title: Artifact regression traceback — scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Observed: 2025-10-28 09:12 UTC - automatic canary rollout (canary-2025Q4.7) started for web-api service.
- Failure: by 09:18 UTC, 2/3 canary pods unhealthy, traffic routed back to stable; partial 502/503 spikes.
- Suspect: artifact promotion race / wrong digest pinned to canary tag (image immutability issue).

Quick timeline (notes captured live):
- 09:10: trigger: ci-release/job/ship-v2025q4 -> promoted tag: v2025q4-canary (lightweight promotion step)
- 09:12: k8s rollout started (deployment/canary-web-api)
- 09:14: first CrashLoopBackOff on canary-1
- 09:16: health check flapping, service returning 502s -> rollback triggered by SRE guardrail
- 09:25: canary rollback complete, incidents quiet after 09:28

Commands run (copied from terminal):
- gcloud builds list --filter="images:projects/redwood-releases" --limit=5  # checked build timeline
- gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-release-artifacts/2025Q4/web-api/  # list artifacts for digest check
- docker pull gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api:v2025q4-canary && docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api:v2025q4-canary
- curl -sS -D - http://canary-web-api-1.internal:8080/health  # flapping checks returned 502/200 alternating
- kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=web-api -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl describe pod canary-web-api-1 -n prod  # events show failed liveness probe and repeated OOMKilled? (see logs)
- kubectl logs canary-web-api-1 -n prod --previous  # crash stack trace below
- gcloud container images describe gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:abcdeffedcba1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345

Error snippets captured:
- kubernetes events:
  Warning  Unhealthy  1m (x12 over 4m)  kubelet  Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.20.3.5:8080/health": dial tcp 10.20.3.5:8080: connect: connection refused

- container stderr (truncated):
  ERROR 2025-10-28T09:14:21Z service.bootstrap  - artifact verification failed: expected digest sha256:abcdeff... got sha256:def1234...
  FATAL 2025-10-28T09:14:22Z main  - cannot start: artifact integrity mismatch

- CI logs (ci-release/job/ship-v2025q4):
  [09:08:51] promote-artifact.sh --tag v2025q4-canary --source=gcr.io/dev-outputs/web-api:latest
  [09:09:02] promote-success  (returned 0)
  [09:09:03] update-k8s-manifests --image gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api:v2025q4-canary --apply
  # BUT: earlier build that generated the canary tag shows two different digests within 10s window

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Promotion race: two artifacts were pushed within the promotion window; the tag v2025q4-canary pointed at digest D1 when we updated manifests, but the deployed nodes pulled digest D2 because registry tag was moved after manifest update. Runtime verifies embedded artifact digest against a build-time manifest and fails.
2) Immutable builds broken: CI step used floating 'latest' as source incorrectly; promotion script didn't pin digest when writing k8s manifest.
3) Image pull discrepancy: some nodes pulled from mirror (internal registry cache) which was stale / partially replicated leading to mixed digests across pods.
4) New startup check introduced in 2025-10-25 commit added strict digest verification which surfaces the mismatch.

Evidence supporting 1/2:
- inspect of gcr image by digest vs tag:
  $ gcloud container images describe gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api:v2025q4-canary --format=json
returns: "image_summary": {"digest": "sha256:def1234..."}
  but build artifacts bucket contains a file named manifest-v2025q4-canary.json with expected_digest: sha256:abcdeff... (different)
- promote-artifact.sh log shows two registry pushes at 09:08:46 and 09:08:57 -> possible overwrite of tag

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- pinned rollout to digest: patched deployment to use gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:abcdeff... and kubectl apply -f patched-deploy.yaml -n prod -> pods with pinned digest still fail with same digest mismatch (weird)
- rolled back to stable image gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:0011223344 -> stable pods healthy
- invalidated internal registry cache on mirror-01 (internal step), restarted containerd on two affected nodes
- triggered manual re-pull on node: sudo crictl pull gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:abcdeff... -> pull succeeded, digest matches locally

Outstanding anomalies / questions:
- Why did pinned digest pod still fail with the same "expected abcdeff got def1234" after we patched manifest to pin abcdeff? Possibilities:
  - runtime is reading a different artifact verification manifest from mounted configmap (not k8s image digest) -> check configmap/artifact-manifest used by entrypoint
  - startup cache contains an old copy baked into the image? (less likely)
  - service has an extra artifact fetch step at startup that pulls secondary assets (wasm, models) from release bucket - those secondary assets may be mismatched.

Follow-up checks to run (todo):
- [ ] check service entrypoint for artifact verification source (grep for "expected_digest" in repo)
- [ ] inspect configmaps mounted into web-api pods: kubectl get cm -n prod -o yaml | grep -A3 artifact-manifest
- [ ] re-run promote-artifact.sh in dry-run with verbose logging; ensure promote writes manifest with pinned digest not tag
- [ ] check registry logs (gcr/audit) for tag movement events between 09:08:40-09:09:10
- [ ] correlate pushes: ci/container-build-4798 vs ci/container-build-4799 (two builds in short window)
- [ ] verify mirror replication status for mirror-01 and mirror-02 for timeframe
- [ ] add temporary guard to promotion that blocks tag movement for 2m until manifests are reconciled

Workarounds considered:
- Force-promotion: lock tag -> patch promote script to use digest-based promotion only (no re-tagging)
- Prevent future races: require builder to create digest file and use that to update k8s manifests atomically (use gitops commit with digest)
- Add preflight job in release pipeline that compares manifest digest to registry digest after promotion (fail fast)

Notes for root-cause doc (put into JIRA RE-4721):
- Include registry push timestamps and digests for both builds.
- Include MD5/sha256 from gs artifact bucket and from image manifest to show mismatch.
- Document that the runtime performs secondary artifact verification (note path: /app/config/artifact-manifest.json) and include its contents.

Commands to copy into JIRA for analysts:
- gsutil cp gs://redwood-release-artifacts/2025Q4/web-api/manifest-v2025q4-canary.json /tmp/ && jq .expected_digest /tmp/manifest-v2025q4-canary.json
- gcloud container images list-tags gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api --filter="tags:v2025q4-canary" --limit=10 --format="get(digest,timestamp)"
- gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND jsonPayload.message:promote-artifact" --freshness=1h --limit=50 --project=redwood-prod

Scratch log (raw lines):
- 09:08:46 PUSH gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:abcdeff (build-4798)
- 09:08:57 PUSH gcr.io/redwood-prod/web-api@sha256:def1234 (build-4799)
- 09:09:02 TAG v2025q4-canary -> sha256:def1234  # potential overwrite
- 09:14:19 pod canary-web-api-1: startup: verifying artifact manifest -> mismatch -> exit 1

Immediate next actions (who/when):
- Tom: pull registry audit logs and attach to JIRA (by EOD)
- Priya: instrument promote-artifact.sh dry-run with --atomic flag and add a git-tag-based commit (tomorrow morning)
- Me (Aisha): add temporary gating to release pipeline to disable moving tags for 5m window and write short postmortem draft (today)

Notes to self: keep this file as ephemeral scratchpad; once RCA is finished move cleaned timeline and commands to JIRA and Confluence.

Misc misc:
- Observed one node still had old containerd cache with only abcdeff present; after crictl pull we had both digests locally. This supports mirror/replication timing issue.
- Consider using digest pinning in kustomize overlays by default (kustomize vars).

End of scratchpad.
